symptom:
A small TCP key-value server (server/main.go) appends every PUT as a checksummed key=value line to data/kv.log, fsyncs, and only then answers OK. On start it reads the log back, verifies each record and rebuilds its in-memory map. The client remembers every PUT that was answered OK and reads them all back at the end.

Observed on seed 1: the client was partitioned from the server at 292ms, the server was crashed during a disk operation at 757ms and again at 1.7s. The client reported: acknowledged write lost: k14=v14, server now answers "NONE". Every PUT in the run had been answered OK after the server's fsync call returned success.

Expected: every PUT that returned OK must be readable after crashes and restarts.
